conclusion: Ontic indeterminacy associated with superluminal transformations cannot originate from finite information, suggesting that such theories require unbounded informational content akin to deterministic classical theories.

title: Wave Packet Motion In A Quantized Electromagnetic Field: Analytic Results
authors: Szabolcs Hack, Béla Gábor Pusztai, Krisztina Joós, Sándor Varró, Attila Czirják And Péter Földi
abstract: We investigate the dynamics of a charged particle interacting with a multimode quantized electromagnetic field and obtain an analytic solution for the full electron-field system. In the present finite-mode formulation the total electron-field dynamics remains closed and unitary. The framework enables the calculation of position expectation values and uncertainties for arbitrary wave packets and field states, allowing us to identify quantum corrections to the corresponding classical motion. While the corrections to the position expectation value are weak and largely insensitive to the quantum state of the field, the wave packet broadening exhibits a pronounced dependence on the field state. In particular, the quantum uncertainty of the radiation is directly imprinted onto the spatial uncertainty of the particle. We illustrate these effects for Gaussian wave packets interacting with coherent, Fock, and squeezed states, including bright squeezed vacuum. The interaction with a finite-duration laser pulse is also analyzed as a multimode example. Our results provide a transparent analytic route toward understanding how quantum fluctuations of light influence electron dynamics in strong-field settings.
tldr: This paper analytically solves the dynamics of a charged particle interacting with a quantized electromagnetic field, showing how quantum field fluctuations affect electron motion.
motivation: To understand how quantum fluctuations of light influence electron dynamics in strong-field settings, which is important for quantum optics and strong-field physics.
method: The authors derive an analytic solution for the full electron-field system in a finite-mode formulation, computing position expectation values and uncertainties for arbitrary wave packets and field states.
result: Quantum corrections to the position expectation value are weak and insensitive to the field state, but wave packet broadening strongly depends on the field state, with quantum uncertainty of the radiation imprinted onto the particle's spatial uncertainty.
conclusion: The work provides a transparent analytic route to understanding quantum light-matter interactions, but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems as defined in the research interests.

title: Cavity-induced Multispin Interactions And Phase Transitions In Ultracold Fermi Gases
authors: Shi-Liang Zhu And Z D Wang Zhen Zheng
abstract: The many-body physics of higher-spin systems is expected to host qualitatively new matter phases, but realizing them requires the controllable interactions between multispin components that can be tuned independently for each component. Here we propose a scheme that meets this demand in ultracold Fermi gases. By engineering the atom-cavity coupling, we generate cavity-induced effective interactions between pseudo-spin states via multiple Raman and cavity paths. Focusing on the simplest spin-1 case, we obtain two independent scattering channels whose relative strengths and signs are determined by the Clebsch–Gordan coefficients and optical-field parameters. The resulting Hamiltonian combines the on-site Cooper pairing with the off-site repulsion, and drives a continuous transition from the superfluid to the spin-density-wave phase. The coexistence region is reminiscent of a supersolid, yet the self-organized modulation appears in the spin density profile of a higher-spin representation, rather than in the number density profile. The proposal can be implemented with the existing techniques in ultracold atoms. Therefore it offers a versatile platform for quantum simulation of higher-spin many-body physics.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to realize cavity-induced multispin interactions in ultracold Fermi gases, enabling quantum simulation of higher-spin many-body physics.
motivation: Higher-spin systems can host novel quantum phases, but realizing controllable multispin interactions is challenging.
method: By engineering atom-cavity coupling via multiple Raman and cavity paths, effective interactions between pseudo-spin states are generated, with independent control over scattering channels.
result: For spin-1, two independent scattering channels are obtained, leading to a Hamiltonian with on-site Cooper pairing and off-site repulsion, driving a continuous superfluid to spin-density-wave phase transition with a supersolid-like coexistence region.
conclusion: The scheme is experimentally feasible with existing ultracold atom techniques and provides a versatile platform for simulating higher-spin many-body physics.

title: Observation Of Alignment Tensor Effects In Metastability-exchange Collisions With Highly Polarized 3 ...
authors: Yida Sha, Kaiwen Yi, Xingqing Jin, Matteo Fadel And Xiang Peng
abstract: Highly polarized ensembles prepared by metastability-exchange optical pumping (MEOP) have been widely used in precision measurements and fundamental physics. Metastability-exchange (ME) collisions, serving as the basis of MEOP, are traditionally described in terms of atomic orientation, while the significant contributions of metastable alignment tensor at high polarization remain unexplored. In this work, we develop a linearized model under mean-field approximation to investigate alignment tensor effects in highly polarized , which originate from the metastable manifold and are revealed through ME-induced relaxation and frequency shift. By means of free-induction-decay measurements, a pronounced dependence on nuclear polarization is experimentally observed in the response of the ground-state-metastable hybrid ensembles to the external magnetic field. Furthermore, after obtaining the characteristics of tensor-induced phenomena, we demonstrate good agreement between the experiment and the theory. This work advances the understanding of nuclear spin dynamics in highly polarized using MEOP. It further provides applications in systematic error correction of high-accuracy magnetometry, as well as in optimal protocol for the generation of nuclear spin-squeezed states.
tldr: This paper studies alignment tensor effects in metastability-exchange collisions with highly polarized 3He, focusing on nuclear spin dynamics and magnetometry applications.
motivation: To understand and model the previously unexplored alignment tensor contributions in metastability-exchange collisions at high polarization, which affect relaxation and frequency shifts.
method: A linearized mean-field model is developed and validated through free-induction-decay measurements on hybrid ground-state-metastable ensembles.
result: A pronounced dependence of the ensemble response on nuclear polarization is observed, and the model shows good agreement with experiment.
conclusion: The work advances understanding of nuclear spin dynamics in highly polarized 3He and provides applications for systematic error correction in magnetometry and generation of spin-squeezed states.

title: Exploring Exotic Spin-dependent Interactions Beyond The Standard Model: Theoretical Foundations And Experimental Investigations
authors: L Y Wu And H Yan
abstract: New interactions mediated by novel particles propose solutions to several important questions in modern physics. Axions serve as examples of such particles; they are lightweight and interact weakly with ordinary matter. This category of particles, including those similar to axions—termed axion-like particles (ALPs)—arises from diverse theoretical frameworks, such as the Peccei-Quinn mechanism addressing the strong CP problem, string theory, and spontaneous supersymmetry breaking. Given their light mass and weak coupling, ALPs are also possible candidates for cold dark matter. Introducing these new interactions mediated by novel particles not only tackles several challenges in modern physics but also raises a crucial question: Are there undiscovered interactions beyond the standard model (SM)? Many of the interactions predicted by these theories are spin-dependent, which is the primary focus of this review. In this review, we first outline the theoretical foundations for investigating exotic spin-dependent interactions, highlighting their importance in various models beyond the SM. We examine the potential roles of new lightweight particles in mediating these interactions, which may enhance our understanding of dark matter. Relevant formulas derived from theoretical models are included to support experimental investigations. Following this theoretical framework, we conduct a detailed review of recent experimental efforts to detect these exotic interactions. A systematic review of current constraints on these interactions is presented, along with an assessment of various detection approaches.
tldr: A review of exotic spin-dependent interactions mediated by axion-like particles, covering theoretical foundations and experimental searches.
motivation: To explore new physics beyond the Standard Model, including dark matter candidates, through spin-dependent interactions.
method: Theoretical derivation of interaction potentials and systematic review of experimental constraints from various detection approaches.
result: Compilation of current experimental bounds on exotic spin-dependent interactions and assessment of detection methods.
conclusion: Exotic spin-dependent interactions remain an active area of research with potential implications for dark matter and fundamental physics.

title: Observation Of Floquet Tensor Monopoles
authors: Hao Yuan, Weixuan Zhang, Na Sun And Xiangdong Zhang
abstract: Tensor monopoles, topological singularities of Kalb–Ramond tensor gauge fields, have garnered widespread attention in high-energy and condensed matter physics. They give rise to exotic phenomena such as quantized magnetoelectric responses and chiral boundary states, acting as potential building blocks for the development of topological devices in high-dimensional space. However, theoretical studies and experimental realizations reported to date have remained in static settings, and the realization of Floquet tensor monopoles (FTMs) and their associated anomalous non-equilibrium topological features has yet to be achieved. Here, we report the first theoretical and experimental implementation of FTMs in a four-dimensional non-equilibrium system. We systematically uncover the driving-frequency controlled creation, motion, and annihilation of FTMs, together with their anomalous bulk-edge correspondence. These phenomena are unique to FTMs and have no static counterparts. In experiments, we design and fabricate time-varying topological circuits, and directly observe the controllable motion of FTMs in k-space and their induced 3D Fermi-arc surface states by tuning the driving frequency. Our findings extend tensor monopole research to the non-equilibrium regime, providing a theoretical and experimental platform for exploring exotic topological phases in dynamic tensor gauge fields and laying the groundwork for functional topological devices with real-time control.
tldr: This paper reports the first experimental observation of Floquet tensor monopoles in a four-dimensional non-equilibrium system, extending tensor monopole research to the non-equilibrium regime.
motivation: Tensor monopoles have been studied in static settings, but their non-equilibrium counterparts and associated anomalous topological features have not been realized.
method: The authors design and fabricate time-varying topological circuits to realize a four-dimensional non-equilibrium system, and observe the creation, motion, and annihilation of Floquet tensor monopoles by tuning the driving frequency.
result: They directly observe controllable motion of Floquet tensor monopoles in k-space and their induced 3D Fermi-arc surface states.
conclusion: This work provides a platform for exploring exotic topological phases in dynamic tensor gauge fields and lays groundwork for functional topological devices with real-time control.

title: Pseudo-Hermitian Magnon Dynamics
authors: Xi-Guang Wang And Jamal Berakdar
abstract: A defining quantity of a physical system is its energy which is represented by the Hamiltonian. In closed quantum mechanical or/and fully coherent wave-based systems the Hamiltonian is introduced as a Hermitian operator which ensures real energy spectrum and secures the decomposition of any state over a complete basis set that spans the space where states live. Pseudo-Hermitian, or PT symmetric, systems are a special class of non-Hermitian ones. They describe open systems but may still have real energy spectrum. The eigenmodes are however not orthogonal in general. This qualitative difference to Hermitian physics has a range of consequences for the physical behavior of the system in the steady state or when it is subjected to external perturbations. This overview reviews the recent progress in the field of pseudo-Hermitian physics as it unfolds when applied to low-energy excitations of magnetically ordered materials. The focus is mainly on long wavelength spin excitations (spin waves) with magnons being the energy quanta of these excitations. Various setups including ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, magnonic crystals, and hybrid structures with different types of coupling to the environments as well as spatio-temporally engineered systems will be discussed with a focus on the particular aspects that are brought about by the pseudo-Hermiticity such as mode amplification, non-reciprocal propagation, magnon cloaking, non-Hermitian skin effect, PT-symmetric assisted Floquet engineering, topological energy transfer, and field-induced enhanced sensitivity.
tldr: A review of pseudo-Hermitian magnon dynamics in magnetically ordered materials, focusing on non-Hermitian effects such as mode amplification and non-reciprocal propagation.
motivation: To survey recent progress in pseudo-Hermitian physics applied to magnonic systems, highlighting unique phenomena arising from non-orthogonal eigenmodes.
method: The paper is a review that discusses various theoretical and experimental setups, including ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, magnonic crystals, and hybrid structures, with emphasis on pseudo-Hermiticity.
result: Key phenomena include mode amplification, non-reciprocal propagation, magnon cloaking, non-Hermitian skin effect, PT-symmetric Floquet engineering, topological energy transfer, and enhanced sensitivity.
conclusion: Pseudo-Hermitian magnonics is a rapidly developing field with potential for novel applications, but the paper does not present new results or directly advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: On The Significance Of Wigner’s Friend In Contexts Beyond Quantum Foundations
authors: Caroline L. Jones And Markus P. Mueller
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2147 (2026).

There has been a surge of recent interest in the Wigner's Friend paradox, sparking several novel thought experiments and no-go theorems. The main narrative has been that Wigner's Friend highlights a counterintuitive feature that is unique to quantum theory, and which is closely related to the quantum measurement problem. Here, we challenge this view. We argue that the gist of the Wigner's Friend paradox can be reproduced without assuming quantum physics, and that it underlies a much broader class of enigmas in the foundations of physics and philosophy. To show this, we first consider several recently proposed Extended Wigner's Friend scenarios, and demonstrate that some of their implications for the absoluteness of observations can be reproduced by classical thought experiments that involve the duplication of agents. Crucially, some of these classical scenarios are technologically much easier to implement than their quantum counterparts. Then, we argue that the essential structural ingredient of all these scenarios is a feature that we call "Restriction A": that a physical theory cannot give us a probabilistic description of the observations of all agents. Finally, we argue that this difficulty is at the core of other puzzles in the foundations of physics and philosophy, and demonstrate this explicitly for cosmology's Boltzmann brain problem. Our analysis suggests that Wigner's Friend should be studied in a larger context, addressing a frontier of human knowledge beyond quantum foundations: to obtain reliable predictions for experiments in which these predictions can be privately but not intersubjectively verified.

.
tldr: The paper argues that the Wigner's Friend paradox is not unique to quantum theory but can be reproduced classically, and relates it to broader foundational puzzles like the Boltzmann brain problem.
motivation: To challenge the view that Wigner's Friend highlights a uniquely quantum feature and to show its relevance to foundational issues beyond quantum mechanics.
method: The authors analyze extended Wigner's Friend scenarios, construct classical analogues with agent duplication, and identify a common structural feature called 'Restriction A'.
result: They demonstrate that some implications of Wigner's Friend can be reproduced classically, and that the core issue is a limitation on probabilistic descriptions of all agents' observations.
conclusion: Wigner's Friend should be studied in a broader context addressing privately but not intersubjectively verifiable predictions, extending beyond quantum foundations.

title: Switchable Band Alignment In 2D-perovskite/WS2 Heterostructures For Tunable Exciton Transport And Valley Polarization
authors: Yingying Chen, Zeyi Liu, Zisheng Gong, Cheng Wang, Wendian Yao, Junze Li, Ti Wang, Weibo Gao And Dehui Li
abstract: Van der Waals heterostructures integrated by two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) hold great potential for engineering promising exciton phenomena, particularly interlayer excitons (IXs) featuring extended lifetimes and permanent out-of-plane electric dipole moments. While electrically controllable IX emission has been extensively explored in TMD heterobilayers, reconfiguring their band alignment to achieve selected exciton states and exploit these states for novel excitonic functionalities remains an urgent challenge. Here, we demonstrate dynamic exciton control by electrically tunable band alignment transitions between type-II and type-I configurations in WS2/(iso-BA)2PbI4 heterostructures, enabling reversible conversion between charged interlayer (IX±) and charged intralayer (X−) excitons. By tailoring these exciton states, we achieve two critical functionalities: (i) 7 μm ON/OFF control of exciton transport via transition between delocalized IX± (ON) and confined X− (OFF) states; (ii) valley polarization switching with a 16.3 ON/OFF ratio, leveraging distinct spin-valley configurations of IX± (unpolarized) and X− (polarized). Unlike twist-angle-dependent TMD heterobilayers, this platform operates independently of stacking alignment, establishing a broadly hybrid 2D system as a practical paradigm towards programmable nanophotonic circuits.
tldr: This paper demonstrates electrically tunable band alignment in 2D-perovskite/WS2 heterostructures for controlling exciton transport and valley polarization.
motivation: To achieve dynamic control over exciton states and functionalities in van der Waals heterostructures, enabling programmable nanophotonic circuits.
method: The authors fabricate WS2/(iso-BA)2PbI4 heterostructures and apply an electric field to switch between type-II and type-I band alignments, converting between charged interlayer and intralayer excitons.
result: They achieve 7 μm ON/OFF control of exciton transport and valley polarization switching with a 16.3 ON/OFF ratio.
conclusion: This platform offers a twist-angle-independent approach to reconfigurable exciton control, suitable for nanophotonic applications.

title: Non-spreading Meronic Spin Defects Around Optical Vortices
authors: Miguel A Porras And Yijie Shen Nilo Mata-Cervera
abstract: Optical vortices are singularity lines where the light field intensity vanishes and its phase is undefined. These threads of darkness are adorned by Gauss’s law as lines of pure longitudinal polarization where the polarization plane tilts and winds around. The resulting spin field is as a unique structure with both features of topological texture and defect, as it includes a point defect of undefined spin enclosed by a meronic texture which spans half the spin unit sphere. This topological structure does not spread in propagation: the normalized spin field maintains a deep-subwavelength confinement around the vortex line while the underlying vortex beam continues to diffract. From their intrinsic nature and subwavelength confinement, these textures exhibit enhanced robustness upon isotropic perturbations such as atmospheric turbulence compared with other tailored polarization textures. Here we describe these topologies of transverse spin which decorate the phase singularity of paraxial vortex beams, highlighting the diversity of topological structures that arise in two different spaces—the spin unit sphere and the transverse-axial Poincaré sphere—and discuss the underlying aspects behind their subwavelength localization.
tldr: This paper studies topological spin textures around optical vortices, focusing on meronic defects and subwavelength confinement.
motivation: To understand and characterize the unique spin structures that decorate phase singularities in paraxial vortex beams.
method: Theoretical analysis of the spin field topology, including meronic textures and their propagation properties, with numerical simulations.
result: The normalized spin field remains subwavelength confined and exhibits enhanced robustness against perturbations like atmospheric turbulence.
conclusion: These non-spreading meronic spin defects are a novel topological feature of optical vortices with potential applications in robust light-matter interactions.

title: A Less-for-more Metamaterial Paradigm Via Laplace-Helmholtz Correspondence
authors: Zihang Guo, Fubao Yang, Tong Li, Shuihua Yang, Cheng-Wei Qiu, Jingjing He And Liujun Xu
abstract: The Laplace and Helmholtz equations dominate two fundamentally distinct physical processes: steady diffusion with a single constitutive parameter versus dynamic wave propagation with two. Manipulating complex wave dynamics through simple steady fields is typically deemed infeasible. Here, we bridge this gap by establishing the Laplace-Helmholtz correspondence, enabling a ‘less-for-more’ paradigm for metamaterial design. Rooted in a wave invariant, this framework allows the rigorous derivation of the two parameters and oscillatory field for the Helmholtz equation (the ‘more’) solely from the single parameter and steady field of the Laplace equation (the ‘less’). We demonstrate this capability by unlocking functionalities previously considered intractable, such as hyperbolic invisibility and three-dimensional freeform conformal cloaking with broadband performance. We further experimentally validate our strategy via a waveguide cloak. Our results bridge static and dynamic physics, establishing a versatile gateway for manipulating waves beyond conventional constraints.
tldr: This paper establishes a mathematical correspondence between Laplace and Helmholtz equations to design metamaterials for wave manipulation using static fields.
motivation: To bridge static and dynamic physics, enabling complex wave functionalities (e.g., cloaking) through simpler steady-state design.
method: The authors derive a wave invariant that maps the single-parameter Laplace equation to the two-parameter Helmholtz equation, allowing wave field reconstruction from static solutions.
result: They demonstrate hyperbolic invisibility and 3D freeform conformal cloaking with broadband performance, validated experimentally with a waveguide cloak.
conclusion: The Laplace-Helmholtz correspondence provides a versatile paradigm for metamaterial design, overcoming conventional constraints between static and wave physics.

title: A Comprehensive Review On Master Stability Functions In Complex Network Dynamics
authors: Priodyuti Pradhan And Chandrakala Meena Suman Acharyya
abstract: Synchronization is a fundamental emergent phenomenon observed across a wide range of natural and engineered systems. Understanding the stability of a synchronization phenomenon is crucial for ensuring functionality in various complex systems. The master stability function (MSF) framework has emerged as a powerful and elegant tool for analyzing the stability of synchronization in coupled dynamical systems. By separating the effects of the node dynamics from the network structure, the MSF offers deep insights into synchronization behavior. However, a major challenge lies in determining the MSF for complex dynamical networks driven by nonlinear interaction mechanisms. These mechanisms introduce additional complexity due to the intricate connectivity of the interacting elements and the complex dynamics governed by nonlinear processes, diverse parameters, and the higher dimensionality of the system. Although MSF analysis has been widely used for more than past 25 years, a comprehensive and systematic investigation of MSF across various networked systems is still lacking. In this article, we present a simplified and unified analysis for the MSF in various undirected and directed networked systems. We begin by formulating the MSF framework in pairwise coupled identical systems and extend our analysis to directed networks and multilayer networks, considering both intralayer and interlayer interactions. Furthermore, we analyze the MSF formalism for higher-order networks. To facilitate understanding, we complement the theoretical developments with numerical analysis of synchronization stability in coupled systems. We also propose algorithms for computing the MSF, identifying stability regimes, and classifying the MSF behaviors. Overall, the primary goal of this review is to present a systematic study of the MSF in various coupled dynamical networks in a clear and structured manner, making this powerful tool more accessible. Furthermore, we highlight underexplored areas in the application of the MSF and discuss emerging directions, such as estimating the MSF using machine learning approaches.
tldr: A comprehensive review of master stability function framework for synchronization stability in complex networks, covering pairwise, directed, multilayer, and higher-order networks.
motivation: Synchronization is a fundamental emergent phenomenon in natural and engineered systems, and understanding its stability is crucial. The master stability function (MSF) is a powerful tool, but a systematic investigation across various networked systems is lacking.
method: The paper formulates the MSF framework for pairwise coupled identical systems, extends it to directed and multilayer networks with intralayer and interlayer interactions, and analyzes higher-order networks. It also proposes algorithms for computing MSF and classifying stability regimes.
result: Provides a unified analysis of MSF for various undirected and directed networked systems, including numerical examples and algorithms for stability classification.
conclusion: The review systematically presents MSF analysis for diverse coupled dynamical networks, making the tool more accessible, and highlights underexplored areas and future directions like machine learning-based MSF estimation.

title: Hierarchically Discriminating Haar-randomness In Quantum States From A Black-box Device
authors: Hao Wang And Adrián Pérez-Salinas Xavier Bonet-Monroig
abstract: The concept of randomness in quantum computing has been central to constructing benchmarking tools, cryptographic protocols, as well as a proof of beyond-classical computation. Discerning whether quantum states (or unitaries) are randomly distributed is a computational task that requires an enormous amount of quantum computational resources. This work addresses such a challenge by introducing a hierarchical discrimination algorithm to efficiently test if a set of states generated from a black-box quantum device with an unknown distribution is (in)compatible with a random distribution. To this end, we reduce the complexity of the problem by selecting an observable with known spectrum to study the statistical properties of its expectation values with respect to the quantum states from an unknown (black-box) quantum device. Concurrently, we use our first technical result, a connection between Haar-randomness and the Dirichlet distribution, to analytically compute Haar-random moments of the observable. Our Haar-random discriminator test is then simply to compare those statistical moments, such that if fails the test, it is enough to state that the quantum device does not output randomly distributed states. Else, we can not (yet) confirm that the states follow a Haar-random distribution. We further provide an extension to this algorithm by permutation- and unitary-equivalent randomization of the observable at increasing computational resources, which allows us to more accurately state whether is compatible with Haar-randomness. We envision the use of the discriminator test as a quantum device benchmark, by discriminating whether the states generated are incompatible with Haar-randomness.

title: Broadband High-gain Metalens Design Based On Dispersion Compensation
authors: Yanwei Wang, Chuanfei Li, Zhuo Liu And Yunsheng Guo
abstract: Broadband metasurface focusing is often limited by unit-cell phase dispersion and phase–amplitude coupling, leading to degraded performance near the band edges in conventional geometrical-optics (GO) designs. To address this challenge, an inverse-design method combining an artificial neural network and particle swarm optimization is proposed. The unit-cell response is modeled in the complex domain to avoid phase-wrapping discontinuities, while a frequency-dependent aperture reference phase is globally optimized to balance phase accuracy and transmittance. Based on this method, a broadband metalens operating from 9.0 to 10.2 GHz (12.5%) is designed and fabricated. Measured results agree well with simulations and demonstrate a gain enhancement of up to 4.36 dBi over a conventional GO design, with a peak gain of 23.8 dBi. Compared with the feed antenna alone, the maximum gain improvement reaches 16.05 dBi, while the half-power beamwidth is reduced by up to at 10.2 GHz. The proposed method provides an effective route for broadband high-gain metalens design under practical unit-cell constraints.
tldr: This paper presents an inverse-design method for broadband high-gain metalens antennas using neural networks and particle swarm optimization.
motivation: Broadband metasurface focusing is limited by unit-cell phase dispersion and phase-amplitude coupling, degrading performance near band edges in conventional designs.
method: An artificial neural network models the unit-cell response in the complex domain to avoid phase-wrapping discontinuities, and particle swarm optimization globally optimizes a frequency-dependent aperture reference phase.
result: A metalens operating from 9.0 to 10.2 GHz achieves up to 4.36 dBi gain enhancement over conventional design, with peak gain of 23.8 dBi and reduced half-power beamwidth.
conclusion: The proposed method provides an effective route for broadband high-gain metalens design under practical unit-cell constraints.

title: Steady-state Entanglement Harvesting For Two Rotating Atoms In A Cylindrical Cavity
authors: Hong-Tao Zheng, Xiang-Fa Zhou, Guang-Can Guo And Zheng-Wei Zhou
abstract: We study the entanglement dynamics of two rotating atoms (with two internal levels and ) in a cylindrical cavity, which interact with a massless scalar field in vacuum satisfying the Dirichlet boundary condition. Our analysis demonstrates that it is possible to obtain the steady-state entanglement under two types of resonant conditions. For two identical atoms with the same world-line, the system reduces to the usual dissipative Dicke model at the first resonant condition where and are the energy splitting and the angular velocity of the th atom, and is the Lorentz factor. The entangled steady-state takes the form where and are constant, which is consistent with the previous study (see 2022 Phys. Rev. D 106 105028). For two atoms with different world-lines, the system suffers from a significant mixed joint dissipation process at the second resonant condition , and reaches an entangled steady-state as . Moreover, with the help of the cavity, we can obtain a much higher concurrence in the final states by changing the relative ratio of the two orbital radii. Our work thus provides a more effective way for the extraction of steady-state entanglement from the vacuum via the analogue Unruh effect for two rotating atoms in a cylindrical cavity.
